I can't create files without a tool, and you asked me not to use any. Below are both files in full, ready to save as `layout.md` and `CLAUDE.md`. I can write them to disk if you lift that restriction.

## layout.md

| Location | Mechanism | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| `/CLAUDE.md` | Always-loaded memory | Holds only what applies to every task in the repo: org conventions and pointers to the service files. |
| `api/CLAUDE.md` | Nested CLAUDE.md, loaded on demand | The `api/gen/` warning only matters when Claude works in Go code, so it stays out of web and pipeline sessions. |
| `.claude/settings.json` (hook) | PreToolUse hook that blocks Edit/Write on `api/gen/**` | A silent overwrite is costly, and a hook enforces the rule deterministically where a CLAUDE.md line is only advisory. |
| `web/CLAUDE.md` | Nested CLAUDE.md | Tells Claude to use `npm run test:unit` and avoid `npm test`, which launches real browsers via Playwright. |
| `.claude/settings.json` (permissions) | `deny`/`ask` rule for `Bash(npm test:*)` | Stops an accidental browser launch even if the instruction is missed. |
| `pipeline/CLAUDE.md` | Nested CLAUDE.md | Documents that `AIRFLOW_HOME` must be `pipeline/.airflow` before any DAG import, check, or test. |
| Incident-response runbook | Skill (`incident-response/SKILL.md`), distributed through a shared org plugin | Twenty steps used identically company-wide are a procedure to load on demand, not always-on context. A shared plugin keeps one copy for all teams, and atlas enables it via `enabledPlugins`. |
| Warehouse SQL for analysts | MCP server in `.mcp.json`, with read-only credentials from env vars and permissions scoped to its query tool | Live queries need a tool connection, not prose. A read-only role limits what a bad query can do. |
| Metric definitions (optional) | Skill (`product-metrics`) that sits next to the MCP server | Keeps table and metric semantics out of the root file and loads them only for metrics questions. |
| Org-wide conventions (optional) | Managed-policy CLAUDE.md | If the conventions should apply to every repo in the company, this is the better home. The root file keeps a copy so atlas works on its own. |

Not used: `.claude/rules/` with path globs. Nested CLAUDE.md files already give directory scoping with less indirection. Switch to rules if a quirk needs to follow file patterns that cut across directories.

## CLAUDE.md

```markdown
# atlas

Monorepo with three services:
- `api/`: Go, gRPC
- `web/`: React/TypeScript
- `pipeline/`: Python, Airflow

Service-specific rules live in `api/CLAUDE.md`, `web/CLAUDE.md`, and `pipeline/CLAUDE.md`. They load when you work in those directories.

## Conventions (org-wide)
- Use conventional commits (`feat:`, `fix:`, `chore:`, ...).
- `make check` must pass before any PR is opened.
- Trunk-based development. Do not create long-lived branches; keep branches short and merge to trunk quickly.

## Other context
- Incident response: use the `incident-response` skill. Do not reconstruct the runbook from memory.
- Product metrics: query the warehouse through the configured MCP server. It is read-only.
```
